title: Cyberpunk 2077: the bar of El Coyote Cojo, 4K
intro: Not game screenshots: each picture is an upscaler's raw output from the same recorded game frames, shown with a plain display mapping, without the game's tone mapping, effects or UI.
about:
What you are looking at

Cyberpunk 2077: the bar of El Coyote Cojo (stools, painted floor tiles, neon, haze). We recorded 117 consecutive frames (16 of them shown) of the game's upscaler inputs with a small recording layer between OptiScaler and the upscaler: the rendered picture at 2259x1271 (before upscaling), depth, motion vectors, camera jitter, exposure and frame timing, exactly as the game handed them to the upscaler. Output size 3840x2160 (4K).

How the comparison is made

Every upscaler here is fed the same recorded frames, frame by frame, from the same start, so the only difference between two pictures is the upscaler. The last 16 frames play as an animation (pause with the button or Space); the crop is the same region in every picture.

What is not in these pictures

The game's own tone mapping, color grading, bloom, film grain, sharpening and UI are not applied: those run after the upscaler in the game. The upscaler's linear output is shown with one plain mapping for all (x/(1+x), gamma 2.2), so colors and contrast differ from the game; differences between upscalers are what to look at.

How each upscaler ran

AMD FSR 4.1.2: AMD's FSR 4.1.2 for RX 7000 cards, which gives FSR 4.1.1's picture byte for byte; these pictures come from AMD's own FSR 4.1.1 library. AMD FSR 4.1.2 Lite and this project's two builds ran in this project's local test harness, not AMD's own runtime. 4.1.2-lossy and 4.1.2l-lossy are the lossy builds of release dll-2026-11-22 (RX 7000 archive; under Linux its 4.1.2l-lossy runs its Linux form): they change the picture to run faster. This set also shows the same two builds of the release before, dll-2026-11-05, to compare with.

Timings

The time beside each name is one upscale at 4K (from 2260x1272, a moving scene, two runs each) measured on an RX 7800 XT under Linux (Proton) with this project's timing program, not taken from these clips Timings will differ on Windows, and between GPUs: a different card can rank these upscalers differently.
